statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 14%, inside the low band and below the watch threshold.
recommendation: Conditions describe a completed and orderly trend-up session now sitting inside the CME maintenance halt, with no live price discovery until the 22:00Z Globex reopen. The Nasdaq-100 settled about 56 points below its session high after retracing roughly 425 points from the 29,075.00 futures low, and volatility decayed into the close. The near checkpoints are the Globex reopen at 22:00Z and the European open at 07:00Z. The single narrow danger window is the 12:30-14:00Z August employment report on 4 September, which lands before a three-day US weekend.
headline: Nasdaq-100 settles 29,482.32 (+1.16%) about 56 points under its session high; VIX closes 14.32 and September hike odds fall to roughly even
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,482.32, up 1.16%, inside a 29,160.96-29,538.76 session range, finishing roughly 56 points below the high rather than pinned to it. NQ futures last printed 29,502.25 (+1.08%) into the 21:00Z maintenance halt after trading a 29,075.00-29,584.25 range, so the day contained a genuine early retracement, an advance, and a modest fade into the settle. That is the structure that keeps Tail in the low band despite an unambiguous trend-up day, and it is the same pattern the strategy tolerated well earlier in the week. The driver was policy repricing. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he would be inclined to support holding the target range at the 15-16 September meeting if disinflation continues, and market-implied odds of a September hike fell to roughly 50% from about 63%. The 2-year yield eased to around 4.35% and the 10-year to roughly 4.74-4.77%, well off the multi-year high touched earlier in the week. Breadth was broad rather than narrow: the Dow added 1.18%, the S&P 500 1.06% and the Nasdaq Composite 1.40%, so the advance was not carried by a single megacap. Nvidia disclosed an agreement to acquire Hugging Face for approximately $13 billion in an 8-K filed today, an AI catalyst that was absorbed during cash hours without producing one-way index extension. VIX finished 14.32, down 5.79%, close to its 14.23 session low, which is volatility decay rather than expansion. The unresolved item is energy: WTI near $91.67 and Brent above $95, up more than 7% on the week, as Iran continued strikes on U.S. Gulf allies and Kuwait engaged incoming missiles and drones. That keeps Stress elevated in the mid-50s without establishing an equity-index price path that denies retracement. The forward risk is concentrated in one narrow window: the August employment report at 12:30Z on 4 September, with consensus near +53K to +58K payrolls and the unemployment rate seen holding at 4.1%, followed by the 13:30Z cash open. Forecast dispersion for that print is wide, running from roughly -25K to +121K, and it arrives before a three-day weekend with Labor Day on 7 September. Consistent with prior calibration, event magnitude and dispersion raise Stress and lower Confidence across those hours rather than asserting that a no-retracement path has already formed, so the projected Tail is capped at the top of the watch band through the release and the cash open and decays quickly thereafter if price discovery proves orderly.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 hours the published state was green in 18 of the 21 assessed hours. Tail sat between 11% and 14% through the late US evening, the Asian session and the European morning while Stress drifted from the mid 50s down to 52%. The state moved to yellow at 15:00Z and 16:00Z with Tail at 21% and 20% as the index held its session extreme after the Waller remarks and the ISM Services beat, returned to green at 17:00Z during consolidation, went yellow again at 18:00Z on a fresh session high, then back to green from 19:00Z once that high was retraced and the index settled below it, with Tail easing to 17% by 20:00Z. Three hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The near path keeps Tail in the low band now that the session has settled below its high and the CME maintenance halt has removed live price discovery, easing further through the Globex reopen as participation thins. Risk is projected at an overnight floor through the Asian session and then rebuilds gradually across European hours into the August employment report at 12:30Z on 4 September, which is the mapped danger window through 14:00Z. Tail is deliberately capped at the top of the watch band across the release hour and the US cash open that follows, because event magnitude and forecast dispersion raise Stress and lower Confidence rather than establishing a no-retracement price path. Beyond 14:00Z the projection assumes orderly price discovery and decay back into the low band, with a small Stress rebuild into the Friday close to reflect three-day weekend gap exposure while the Iran-Gulf file is unresolved.
